notes: Data came from the Next.js App Router RSC flight payload embedded in the leaderboard document (self.__next_f), not from a separate XHR/fetch endpoint. list_network_requests filtered to xhr/fetch showed only auth/geo/analytics calls - the site has no public JSON data endpoint on this page. There is no __NEXT_DATA__ element (App Router, not Pages Router).
raw.json is the verbatim `models` array from that payload (634 model entries, ~3.34 MB), unmodified.

The rendered DOM table showed only 289 rows (Status: Current filter) and 15 summary columns. The RSC payload is a strict superset: it includes deprecated/older models and every per-eval score, so no tab or category iteration was needed.
Benchmark display names are a mapping of the payload field keys to their commonly used names; every record keeps the exact original key in `source_field` so nothing is lost or guessed at read time.

MMLU-Pro, AIME and LiveCodeBench are NOT present in this payload - the current Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index eval set on this page consists of the benchmarks listed in benchmarks_captured. No values were invented for missing evals.
`rank` is present only on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index records and is derived by sorting all 621 models that report an index descending; it is not a rank published by the site.

`cost_usd` on every record is the model-level blended price per 1M tokens at a 3:1 input:output ratio (field price1mBlended0To3To1), attached as cost context; it is not a per-benchmark cost. Per-benchmark cost fields existed in the schema but were `$undefined` for the models sampled.
`date` is the model release date (releaseDate) reported by the site, not the scrape date.
Score scales are as published: eval scores are fractions 0-1 (e.g. gpqa 0.5727), index values are on their own scales. No rescaling applied.
Null and `$undefined` values were omitted rather than filled.
